subjectOf.text: The design names a failure pattern in advance: if the likelihood filter, the equal-weight pool, and the reputation pool each carry the negative label against full replacement in every family, the paper issues a registered sentence recording that each had lower capped retention at generation 50 than full replacement, as a registered negative result and not an implementation failure.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: The sentence is available only on the stated pattern of labels in every family.
Naming the pattern in advance is what distinguishes it from a post hoc explanation of a bad result.
